title: Reported fraud losses rose while report volume stayed broadly stable, with loss incidence and severity split by age
source_unit: FTC Consumer Sentinel Network administrative reports
geography: United States reports and reports contributed by partner agencies and organizations

median_fraud_loss_2024.unit: US dollars among reports with loss

observations.method: FTC Consumer Sentinel Network annual administrative report counts and reported-loss summaries.
observations.uncertainty: Reports are unverified, not a population survey, and include multiple data contributors; totals and category definitions can change with late reports and revisions.
observations.subgroup: Fraud, identity-theft, and other Sentinel report types across annual report frames.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher loss share can reflect reporting composition, contributor coverage, or changing scam severity rather than a population-wide incidence change; no denominator of all consumers is available.

observations.period: 2024 fraud reports with usable age information

denominator.unit: 2024 fraud reports with usable age information

age_20_29_median_loss.unit: US dollars among age-20-to-29 reports with loss

age_70_79_median_loss.unit: US dollars among age-70-to-79 reports with loss

observations.method: FTC 2024 Consumer Sentinel age-conditioned fraud-loss table.
observations.uncertainty: Age is reported for only a subset of fraud reports; conditional medians describe reported losses, not age-specific population risk or total harm.
observations.subgroup: Reported fraud by age, especially ages 20–29 and 70–79.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different reporting propensity, scam mix, resources, and exposure can produce the incidence/severity split; the table does not measure digital skill or platform causation.

boundary: This is an administrative report and reported-loss layer, not a prevalence, verified-harm, recovery, or consumer-remedy estimate. It does not follow a person from platform or payment exposure through dispute, recovery, trust, or exit. The retrieval hash will cover the committed analysis memo.
